takeaways.label: Best quarter ever, fivefold profit jump
takeaways.text: PBT and PAT both grew more than 5x YoY, with revenue surging ~144% YoY and ~33% QoQ, driven by hyperscaler data center demand and capacity utilization.

takeaways.label: Order book swells to ₹29,000 crores
takeaways.text: The book grew by ₹3,000 crores in a single quarter despite delivering ₹2,500 crores, implying an order inflow of over ₹5,500 crores.

takeaways.label: Margins expand sharply, more promised
takeaways.text: EBITDA margin hit 25.89%, up 640 bps YoY, and management is confident of further improvement, not just maintenance.

takeaways.label: Guidance raised again, ₹10,000 crore milestone pulled forward
takeaways.text: FY27 revenue growth guidance revised to at least 80%, and the FY29 ₹10,000 crore target is now expected "much sooner."

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether the EPC segment loss reverses as billed milestones clear, the pace of defence revenue ramp toward the ₹500 crore target, and any stabilization in fiber pricing after a ~20% sequential rise.

points.label: Hyperscaler capex is the engine
points.text: ~70% of the ₹18,500 crore OFC and data center interconnect order book comes from hyperscalers for export, and management sees AI as a necessity that will keep data center construction going regardless of interest rate moves.

points.label: Telco demand is waking up
points.text: Telcos, which had stopped buying for two years due to price shocks, are now starting to purchase fiber again, with concrete inquiries being received.

points.label: Geographic diversification still ahead
points.text: Growth has not yet picked up in Europe or Asia ex-China, and management expects this to provide an additional demand layer that would more than offset any slowdown from one or two individual players.

points.label: Pricing has surged, now seen stabilizing
points.text: Prices rose in Q2, and while management expects some further increase, it does not expect the magnitude of prior quarters; the company itself cautions it was wrong on this call last quarter.

points.label: Preform spot market is "insanity"
points.text: Spot preform prices have hit USD 300/kg, up 600%, driven by non-availability; HFCL is insulated via predetermined long-term contracts and does not pay spot.

quotes.text: Nahata: "AI rather than being a luxury or availability to the few, it has become a common requirement and necessity. With that kind of a necessity going around, I don't think there will be any slow down in more data centers coming up in future or in the pace with which they are coming."

sections.title: Optical Fiber & Cable: Capacity, Mix and Margins

points.label: Fiber is fully loaded
points.text: Fiber lines run at 100% of capacity, though throughput varies by type (180-micron data center fiber yields higher price realization but slower draw speeds than 250-micron).

points.label: Cable utilization is full on a revenue basis
points.text: Different cable types run on different machines, so physical utilization varies, but on a money basis the company achieves 100% of envisaged capacity. Data center products run 24/7, while telco cables have somewhat lower demand.

points.label: Product mix is the margin story
points.text: Telecom segment EBITDA margins of 32–33% are attributed to a mix favoring higher-priced data center fiber (A2, 180 micron at ~USD25 per km) over telco fiber (D fiber at ~USD15 per km); data center products require specialized, higher-technology fiber with tighter geometries.

points.label: Capacity expansion underway
points.text: OFC capacity is being expanded from 3.9 crore to 6.3 crore fiber kilometers, focused on in-demand cables like data center products; a 600 MT preform facility covering roughly half of total fiber needs is on track for late CY28, with a mid-term preform cost-reduction solution starting Q1 CY27 that management calls a trade secret.

points.label: Germanium supply being secured early
points.text: The company has started talking to suppliers for needs two years out; germanium is a small percentage of overall cost, so price impact is expected to be minimal.

quotes.text: Nahata: "Well, I'm not only confident of maintaining, but I'm confident of getting it better."

points.label: ₹121 crores loss in Q2, driven by billing delays
points.text: Expenses were incurred on BharatNet work but bills could not be raised because defined milestones have not yet cleared the multi-step verification process involving IEs, BSNL, and the BharatNet authority through a 25-step file process.

points.label: Army AMC contract adds to the gap
points.text: Expenditure is being incurred without offsetting revenue; BSNL is in the final stage of approval, expected in a week or 10 days.

points.label: Restructuring under active consideration
points.text: A board committee with external advice from E&Y is finalizing restructuring recommendations; a board meeting is expected in a week or 10 days, with finalization in another couple of weeks.

points.label: Profitability expected from Q1 FY28
points.text: Management expects the EPC segment to start seeing profit from the first quarter of next financial year.

points.label: Revenue ramp is back-end loaded
points.text: H1 FY27 defence revenue was ~₹80 crores against a full-year aspiration of ~₹500 crores; management states the target is "not an issue" and will surely be achieved, driven by electro-optic sights, Foliage Penetration Radar, and the aerospace acquisition.

points.label: Aerospace acquisition nears close
points.text: The acquisition, carrying an unexecuted order book of ~₹1,600–1,800 crores, is expected to complete in Q3 FY27 itself and will start contributing revenue this quarter.

points.label: Product pipeline advancing
points.text: Thermal Weapon Sights for AK-203 have delivered a second batch; Foliage Penetration Radar has passed its first trial with a second expected in ~2 weeks; the company has bid on a large Drone Detection Radar tender and a tender for 800,000 multi-mode hand grenades.

points.label: Ammunition complex gets land
points.text: The Government of Andhra Pradesh has allotted 1,000 acres; construction will start soon, with revenue expected in about two years.

points.label: Long-term ambition
points.text: FY28 defence revenue is targeted at at least ₹2,000 crores, with a three-year aspiration of ₹5,000 crores, providing a second growth pillar that stabilizes revenue and profit if the fiber market matures in 5–7 years.

quotes.text: Nahata: "So hypothetically, 5, 7 years later, fiber market, if at all stabilizes, then this sector of defense will show us growth. So there are 2 pillars of growth in the Company, which stabilizes the revenue and sustainability of profit or rather increase it when both of the sectors are going good."

points.label: Revenue is ramping from zero
points.text: Q1 connectivity revenue was nil; Q2 is estimated at ~₹300 crores; full-year FY27 target is ₹800 crores, with FY28 projected at ₹2,000 crores.

points.label: Higher-capacity products being introduced
points.text: Revenue from these is expected to start in the last quarter of FY27 or, in a larger way, at the beginning of FY28.

points.label: Already certified and supplying inside data centers
points.text: The company is generating revenue from connectivity solutions within data center environments.

items.title: OFC capacity expansion
items.text: HFCL is adding 0.91 crore fkm of optical fiber and 2.8 crore fkm of OFC capacity by July 2028, taking totals to 4.31 and 6.2 crore fkm respectively, with fiber and OFC utilization at 100%. The ₹1,800 crore capex is funded, and the combined OFC order book of ~₹19,000 crore (70% from hyperscalers) gives multi-year revenue visibility.

items.title: Preform backward integration
items.text: A 600 MT preform facility (₹1,250 crore capex) is being doubled with commissioning accelerated to October 2028, covering half of the 4.5 crore fkm capacity. Own preform is at least 30% cheaper than buying, cutting fiber costs 18-20% and total raw material costs 10-12% - a direct margin uplift management says "would significantly increase our margin profile".

items.title: $1.1 billion hyperscaler contract
items.text: Deliveries have started against the five-year global OFC supply contract with a leading hyperscaler, requiring minimum multi-million fkm annually from CY26 through CY28 with automatic extension to CY30. This single contract - probably the highest ever secured by an Indian telecom company - anchors the export order book and validates HFCL's position in the AI-driven fiber supercycle.

items.title: Aerostructure acquisition
items.text: HASPL is acquiring Defsys's aerostructure business, with net liabilities taken over of ~₹292 crore, bringing a confirmed export order book of ~₹1,570 crore and domestic orders of ~₹110 crore, with completion expected in the current quarter. This transforms defence from ₹300 crore to ~₹2,300 crore in order book overnight, with revenue starting from the current quarter.

items.title: Defence revenue ramp
items.text: Management targets ₹500-600 crore defence revenue in FY27, at least ₹2,000 crore in FY28, and ~₹5,000 crore in three years, from ₹77 crore in FY26. The Andhra Pradesh ammunition complex (1,000 acres, foundation laid May 2026) and radar approvals (foliage penetration radar nearly through) provide the near-term catalysts.

items.title: BharatNet Phase III
items.text: HFCL's total BharatNet contract value stands at ₹7,335 crore, including the ₹2,666 crore UP (West) award from RVNL in June 2026, with 10-year O&M attached. The O&M book of ₹5,000 crore at 15-20% EBITDA margins provides recurring, high-margin revenue for the next decade.
